study: IFIC Food & Health Survey 2025 — US Calibration
source: International Food Information Council (IFIC) Food & Health Survey 2025
methodology: 3,000 US adults ages 18-80, Dynata consumer panel, March 13-27 2025, weighted by age/education/gender/race-ethnicity/region (2024 CPS)

sprint_questions.text: How would you describe your own health, in general?
How stressed have you been over the past 6 months?
In the past year, have you noticed a change in the overall cost of food and beverages?
When shopping for foods and beverages, do you consider whether the food is processed before purchasing that product?

options.A: Yes, and I always avoid processed foods
options.B: Yes, and I sometimes avoid processed foods
options.C: Yes, but I don't avoid processed foods
options.E: I'm not sure what is considered a processed food

sprint_questions.text: Are you familiar with the term 'ultraprocessed food'?
Which of the following best describes your familiarity with the 'Dietary Guidelines for Americans' (US government-approved food and nutrition guidelines)?

options.A: I know a lot about them
options.B: I know a fair amount about them
options.C: I have heard of them, but know very little about them
options.D: I have never heard of them

sprint_questions.text: To what extent do you agree or disagree with the following statement: 'Because nutrition information seems to keep changing, it's hard to know what to believe'
Do you ever replace traditional meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) by snacking or eating smaller meals instead?

options.A: Yes, I regularly replace meals by snacking/smaller meals
options.B: Yes, I occasionally replace meals by snacking/smaller meals
options.C: No, although sometimes I skip meals entirely

sprint_questions.text: In a typical week, how often do you snack or eat something in addition to your main meals?

options.A: Three or more times a day

sprint_questions.text: Overall, how would you grade your diet in terms of healthfulness? (Give it an overall letter grade)
sprint_questions.note: Aggregated from A+/A/A- = 13%, B+/B/B- = 51%, C+/C/C- = 28%, D+/D/D- = 6%, F = 1%

holdout_questions.text: How familiar are you, if at all, with the MyPlate graphic? (the US government's food group visual guide)

options.A: I have seen it and know a lot about it
options.B: I have seen it and know a fair amount about it
options.C: I have seen it, but know very little about it
options.D: I have never seen it before

holdout_questions.text: How, if at all, have you used nutrition information (like calorie counts, etc.) when eating out at restaurants, cafeterias, etc.?

options.A: I will not eat something when eating out without first checking the nutritional information
options.B: I will regularly use nutrition information to decide what to have when eating out
options.C: I will sometimes use nutrition information to decide what to have when eating out
options.D: I have noticed nutrition information before, but haven't paid any attention to it
options.E: I have not noticed or seen any nutrition information when eating out at restaurants

holdout_questions.text: To what extent do you agree or disagree: 'Registered Dietitian Nutritionists are the most qualified experts to provide recommendations on making healthy food choices'
To what extent do you agree or disagree: 'I am more interested in hearing about what TO eat, rather than what NOT to eat'
In the past year, have you come across any content about food or nutrition on social media (e.g., Facebook, Instagram, Pinterest, Twitter/X, YouTube, TikTok)?

options.D: I do not use any social media
